clue.text: Old mathematician in university, one beset by poor grades

indicators.note: to be beset by something is to be surrounded by it, so the grades go round the other pieces

parts.note: E and D are low marks on an exam grading scale
UCL is University College London
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An ancient mathematician at university is plagued by bad exam results.
explanation.walkthrough: 'University' is not U here but UCL, University College London; it and I sit between the poor grades E and D.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek geometer of Alexandria wrote the Elements around 300 BC, so he is an ancient mathematician.

clue.text: Write at length about initially reclusive foreigner?

indicators.note: about means the writing word goes around the letter

parts.note: to expatiate is to speak or write at great length

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of reclusive

explanation.surface: A writer goes on at length about a reclusive foreigner.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone living abroad, away from their homeland, is a foreigner where they live, hence the question mark.

clue.text: My one holds lead of guard dog

indicators.note: holds means the other letters contain the first letter of guard

parts.note: cor is an exclamation of surprise, like 'my!'
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: lead of picks the first letter of guard

explanation.surface: My single dog is held by the lead as a guard dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lead' suggests a dog's leash, but 'lead of' picks the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A short-legged Welsh breed favoured by the Queen is a type of dog.

clue.text: I do not believe in fish being caught by fine line

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the fish is caught, held inside the letters for fine and line

parts.note: F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine
the ide is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: A sceptic doubts that a fish could be landed with a fine fishing line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I do not believe' is what an unbeliever might say, so it serves as the definition; 'in' then supplies the opening letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An unbeliever, one who rejects a faith, could sum up their stance as 'I do not believe'.

clue.text: First bit of news in a month on the radio

definitions.meaning: the first letter of the word news is N, which radio operators call by its code word
the eleventh month of the year

explanation.surface: Early headlines broadcast during a particular month.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the radio' tells you N is to be said the way radio operators spell it, in the NATO phonetic alphabet; that code word is also a month.
explanation.definitionFit: The eleventh calendar month shares its name with the phonetic-alphabet code word for N.

clue.text: It's said to brace individual putting on a little weight

parts.note: oz is the abbreviation for ounce, a little weight
one is a single individual

explanation.surface: Something supposedly bracing helps a person put on a bit of weight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Putting on' sets the ounce in front of the individual. Seaside air has long been called bracing and credited, loosely, to this gas.
explanation.definitionFit: Fresh sea air has been popularly credited with this gas and called bracing.

clue.text: Cover of The Listener?

parts.note: the listener is the ear, and its winter covering keeps it warm, not a magazine cover

explanation.definitionFit: A pad worn over the ear in cold weather covers the organ that listens.

clue.text: Sydney's bored when following only one player in chess club

parts.note: chess has two sides, white and black
in Australian slang to be jack of something is to be fed up with it

explanation.surface: An Australian is bored after playing only one opponent at a chess club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'When following' sets the slang word after the chess colour; 'Sydney's' marks the word as Australian slang.
explanation.definitionFit: A short leather-covered cosh used as a weapon is a club.

clue.text: Reportedly warrants ostentatious luxury

indicators.note: reportedly means the word for warrants is heard rather than seen

parts.note: writs are legal warrants

explanation.surface: Rumoured court warrants for showy extravagance.
explanation.definitionFit: The name of the grand London hotel stands for showy luxury, as in 'putting on the ritz'.

clue.text: White man, note, with one composer

parts.note: an albino is a person lacking pigment, hence white
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A white man jots a note together with a composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Tomaso Albinoni was a Venetian baroque composer, known for the Adagio attributed to him.

clue.text: Case of viral disease surrounding cattle shed from Hertford

indicators.note: surrounding means the disease's letters go around the other piece

parts.note: polio is a viral disease

indicators.note: shed from means the letters of the cattle word are dropped from the town's name

parts.note: a herd is a group of cattle

explanation.surface: A cattle shed in Hertford is the site of an outbreak of a viral disease.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cattle shed' looks like a barn, but 'shed from' says HERD comes out of HERTFORD, leaving RTFO (H, E, R and D removed in order).
explanation.definitionFit: A flat carrying case for papers or drawings goes by this name.

clue.text: Respond, as cast does after rehearsal?

definitions.meaning: to respond is to reply or behave in answer to something
the cast acts the play again

explanation.definitionFit: To respond is to behave in answer to a stimulus, which is the plain sense; the second reading splits it as re- plus act.

clue.text: Encouragement to those whose braces have hitherto come undone?

definitions.text: Encouragement to those whose braces have hitherto come undone?

parts.words: Encouragement to those whose braces have hitherto come undone?
parts.note: a brace is a pair, so someone whose two attempts have failed is told the next one will succeed

explanation.definitionFit: The saying cheers someone on to a further attempt after two failures, and a brace is two.

clue.text: Mentioned explosive agreement that appeals to Cockney consumers

indicators.note: mentioned means said aloud, so the phrase is heard as a sound

parts.note: jelly is slang for gelignite, an explosive, and a deal is an agreement

explanation.surface: A spoken pact over explosives is pitched to London customers.
explanation.walkthrough: A Cockney is a working-class East Londoner; this food is a traditional East End dish.
explanation.definitionFit: The chilled eel in aspic is a classic East End London food sold at pie-and-mash shops.

clue.text: Perfect commentary by croupier, perhaps

definitions.meaning: a card dealer at a casino might announce '...'

explanation.definitionFit: Something perfect is the best imaginable; read as two words it is what a card dealer says.

clue.text: Legless cast's producer emerging from The Globe?

definitions.text: Legless cast's producer emerging from The Globe?

parts.words: Legless cast's producer emerging from The Globe?
parts.note: the cast is a heap of soil left by a burrowing creature with no legs that comes up out of the ground, not actors leaving a theatre

explanation.definitionFit: The creature leaves soil casts and comes out of the earth, the planet called the globe.

clue.text: A singleton should be so pass

definitions.meaning: a person who is single is without a date, read as a phrase of three words

explanation.definitionFit: Passé means old-fashioned, and someone single is literally without a date.

clue.text: Intensive pressure amid unlimited tension in operational locations

indicators.note: amid means the pressure word sits in the middle of the other letters
unlimited means the word loses its outer letters

parts.note: stress is tension
heat is intense pressure, as in 'the heat is on'

explanation.surface: Intense pressure and endless tension in war zones.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unlimited' trims the outer letters of the tension word, leaving TRES; 'amid' sets the pressure word inside that.
explanation.definitionFit: Hospital operating rooms are called theatres, places where operations happen.

clue.text: Blue Tories question university after reshuffle

indicators.note: a reshuffle rearranges a cabinet, so these letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: Conservative politicians quiz a university after a cabinet reshuffle; blue is the Tory colour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blue' fits the Tory surface, since blue is the Conservative party colour, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Turquoise is a greenish-blue colour, named after the gemstone.

clue.text: Britain's weather settling over east European republic

parts.note: UK is Britain, the United Kingdom
rain is a kind of weather

explanation.surface: British weather settles over an eastern European country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Settling over' says RAIN sits over E in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: The country is an independent republic in eastern Europe, capital Kyiv.

clue.text: Sort of joiner left a bumpkin

parts.note: a yoke joins two oxen together

explanation.surface: A carpenter who left town is dismissed as a country rustic.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean an unsophisticated person from the countryside, a rustic.

clue.text: Below which my radar would be at sea?

definitions.text: Below which my radar would be at sea?

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A sailor's radar mounted below the ship's spar would be on the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: radar equipment is hung below this spar on a ship, and 'at sea' also signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: The yardarm is the spar end on a ship's mast, at sea, with gear slung beneath.

clue.text: Lady's fingers cupping cream as corselet hurt bust

indicators.note: bust means broken, so these letters are smashed and rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: A woman's fingers clutch a cream, since her tight corset has hurt her bust.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bust' sits on the corselet surface as a body part, but it is the anagram signal: broken.
explanation.definitionFit: The dessert is a cream or custard set inside a lining of sponge ladyfinger biscuits.

clue.text: Attack where Dad's Armyis seen?

definitions.meaning: an attack or assault, the beginning of something
Dad's Army is a classic British TV sitcom, filmed in a studio

explanation.definitionFit: An onset is an assault, and a TV show is seen on set during filming.

clue.text: Died in prophet's Jewish festival

indicators.note: in means the letter for died goes inside the prophet word

parts.note: a seer is a prophet

explanation.surface: Someone died in a prophet's Jewish feast.
explanation.definitionFit: The ritual meal opening Passover is a Jewish festival observance.

clue.text: Hollow pine kernels turned up in beehive

indicators.note: turned up in a down clue means the letters are read upwards, backwards
hollow means each word is emptied, keeping only its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Empty pine nuts are found turned up in a hive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hollow' keeps PE and KS; 'turned up' reverses PEKS.
explanation.definitionFit: A traditional straw or wicker dome-shaped hive for bees is called this.

clue.text: Returning bird, current native of Australia

indicators.note: returning means the bird's word is read backwards

parts.note: a rook is a bird of the crow family
I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A bird returns, a current native species in Australia.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is an Aboriginal Australian name for an Indigenous person of south-eastern Australia.

clue.text: Fly, fly when riding horse?

indicators.note: the insect is placed inside, as a rider sits in the saddle

parts.note: a saddle horse is one kept for riding, cut here to saddle
a ked is a wingless fly that infests sheep

explanation.surface: Someone flees, swatting at a fly while out on horseback.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'Fly' is the verb, run away; the second is the insect, a sheep parasite, which 'when riding' puts inside the riding seat after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To flee in a hurry, the informal verb for running off.

clue.text: What's sweet yet spicy air found in mine? Oxygen

indicators.note: found in means the air word sits inside the mine word

parts.note: a pit is a coal mine
air in the sense of manner or bearing, a mien
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: Asking what sweet and spicy air is found down a mine, with oxygen supplied.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Air' looks like the breathable kind beside 'Oxygen', but it is MIEN, a person's bearing.
explanation.definitionFit: This sweet red pepper is used to stuff olives and has a mild spiciness.

clue.text: Unconcerned with correctness, bouquet is rejected by Liberal

indicators.note: rejected means turned back, so the scent word is read in reverse

parts.note: a wine's bouquet is its aroma
L is the abbreviation for Liberal, placed beside the reversed scent

explanation.surface: A bunch of flowers is turned down by a Liberal who is careless of propriety.
explanation.definitionFit: Having no moral sense means not caring what is right or wrong.
